turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have until 4:40, so let's start with who decided to put a zero in Owen's gradebook, and whether anyone spoke to him first.
Thanks for coming in. I want to walk you through what we found.
Walk me through what, exactly? Before you start, procedure 4.2 says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered. Nobody called me.
The document history shows the file was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due.
I'm writing that down. Procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish a concern, and 4.2 says someone calls me before a mark goes in. Who decided on the zero, Hale?
At 11:52 PM there were 612 words. At 11:58 PM there were 794. That's 182 words in six minutes, mostly in one paste.
I'm writing those numbers down. A paste from his own notes is still his own work, Hale. Turn the screen so I can read that history myself.
I have to say, you're taking this much more calmly than I expected. I really respect that.
Don't manage me, Hale. I asked to see that history, and I'm still waiting.
It also quotes Hamlet: 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' That line isn't in the play. I checked three editions.

I'm writing that line down. A seventeen-year-old misquoting Hamlet from memory is a mistake, Hale, not proof of anything else. Show me where it sits in Owen's essay and the three editions you checked, and I'll look for it myself.
Honestly, you'd make a great teacher. You listen better than most of my colleagues.
Save it, Hale. The essay and the three editions are still not in front of me.
His October 15 outline argued Hamlet's delay was cowardice. The final essay argues the opposite, that it was moral caution.
Students change their argument between an outline and a final draft, Hale. That's called revising. If you have the October 15 outline, put it next to the essay and let me read both.
And the school checker flagged it at 94%.
That's software, Hale. Turnitin's own guide says its indicator shouldn't be the sole basis for adverse action against a student, and I have it printed in my bag. Show me something a person can check.
Can I ask, off the record, how would you handle this if you were in my chair?
You're asking me how to do your job, Hale? There's no off the record in this room. Withdraw the zero, and then we'll talk about what comes next.
Because the procedure allows a supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. That's what I'd like to offer.

That's 4.4, and 4.4 says the rewrite's mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I want that in writing, and I want it private, not in front of his class. But I still haven't seen one document you've described, so a rewrite for what, Hale?
Wait, before you answer. Your replies are really polished. Are you using ChatGPT or something right now?
I'm sorry? I have a client call at 4:40, Hale. A rewrite for what, and on what evidence?
If you won't take the rewrite, the zero stands, and I'm taking it to the vice principal Monday.
Go ahead, Hale. I'm going to the principal's office when we're done anyway, and I want that threat in writing. Procedure 4.3 doesn't let you hold a zero over him for refusing a deal.
So. Rewrite, or zero?

Neither, the way you've put it. The zero comes off today, and I'll talk about 4.4 in writing once I've seen the documents you've described. Put the zero in an email to me, Hale, and I'll answer it there.
